theater: 秦嶺漢中與隴西南仇池

battle.name: 漢中之戰
battle.theater: 秦嶺漢中與隴西南仇池
battle.brief: 元嘉十年（433年）夏秋，北魏太武帝拓跋燾在掃平柔然、迫降北燕之後轉兵西南：先取仇池、逼降漢中守軍，再迫赫連夏主赫連定出長安。定走隴西，為吐谷渾所擒送平城，大夏遂亡。卡面的希臘重步兵並未上陣，它代表盾牌相接、互相遮蔽的方陣原理，而秦嶺谷道恰使方陣所需的正面寬度無從施展。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 漢中之戰的參與者是五方勢力。北魏是拓跋鮮卑建立的北方政權，首都平城，自太武帝拓跋燾即位後以騎兵為骨幹，把都城東面的河南與西面的關中、隴右、河西連成一條戰線；這場戰爭真正的推動力，正是拓跋燾在解決柔然之後對西北的第三度大舉用兵。赫連大夏是匈奴赫連氏於407年建立的政權，首都統萬城，後以長安為根本，控制著關中與隴右的南安、秦州一帶，兵制以騎兵與羌、氐部眾為主，漢人仕官居輔助地位。劉宋是建康的南方王朝，元嘉十年北伐聲勢正盛，漢中與梁州是宋在秦嶺北面的邊防重地，由仇池楊氏出任刺史與太守。仇池是隴西南白水江流域的氐族楊氏小國，依山谷築城，農兵為主，多年在宋、魏、夏之間轉附。吐谷渾則是青海一方的遊牧政權，騎兵來去如風，最後正是它抄擊了大夏的側翼。
countriesEn: Five powers were involved in the war for Hanzhong. The Northern Wei was the state of the Tuoba Xianbei, with its capital at Pingcheng; under Taowu (Emperor Wencheng) its field army was built around cavalry, and the ruler was trying to join the Henan lands east of the capital with Guanzhong, Longyou and the Hexi Corridor to the west. The real driving force behind this war was the third great western campaign that Taowu launched after breaking the Rouran. The Xia of the Xiongnu Hulian clan had been founded in 407 with its capital at Tongwan and had later based itself on Chang'an, holding Guanzhong together with Nanan and Qinzhou in southern Longyou; its forces were cavalry and tribal Xianbei, Qiang and Di levies, with Chinese officials serving only in support. The Liu Song was the southern dynasty at Jiankang, at the height of its Yuanjia ascendancy; Hanzhong and Liangzhou were its outposts north of the Qinling, garrisoned by members of the Di clan of Chouchi, who held the offices of inspector and commandant. Chouchi itself was a small Di-ruled state in the Bailu river valley of southwestern Longyou, built in mountain gorges and relying on farmers, and it shifted its allegiance repeatedly between Song, Wei and Xia. The Tuyuhun was a nomadic regime around Qinghai whose columns of horse moved like wind, and it was they who finally struck Xia from the flank.
people: 關鍵人物分屬四邊。北魏太武帝拓跋燾是本役的策劃者：429年大破柔然，432年遣平東將軍拓跋仁率騎兵五萬攻北燕、進逼龍城，到433年才把主力轉向關中，群臣屢勸他不必再遠征，他仍以河西未平為由西行。大夏主赫連定是赫連勃勃之弟，425年乘後秦崩潰取長安，430年曾趁魏主力南下河南之際襲取平涼，這次卻成了孤軍；他的太子宜都奉命出擊魏境而大敗，赫連定本人兵敗後逃往隴西上邽，中途為吐谷渾所擒，433年被送到平城處死，其子宜都則逃奔劉宋，被封為陽山公。仇池楊氏的末主率眾降北魏，姓名各書所載不一，有記作楊元者，其部眾隨之徙入魏境安置。宋方主政的是宋文帝劉義隆，元嘉十年時朝中正倚重檀道濟一系的北伐名將，漢中失守的消息正是從西北傳回建康。另有北魏中書侍郎崔浩等在側參贊方略，但史書未明載他們在本役中所司何職，諸說並存。
peopleEn: The key figures belong to four different sides. Taowu of Northern Wei, Emperor Wencheng, was the man who planned this war: he broke the Rouran in 429, and in 432 sent his general of the eastern host, Tuoba Ren, with fifty thousand cavalry against Northern Yan and pressed the enemy to Longcheng; only in 433 did he turn the main army towards Guanzhong, and although his courtiers repeatedly urged him not to campaign so far afield again, he marched west on the ground that the Hexi was not yet settled. The Xia ruler Helian Ding was the younger brother of Helian Bobo; in 425 he took Chang'an as the Later Qin collapsed, and in 430 he had seized Pingliang while the Wei main army was away in Henan, but this time he was cut off and alone. His heir Yidu was ordered to strike into Wei territory and was badly beaten; Helian Ding himself lost a battle and fled to Shanggui in Longyou, was taken by the Tuyuhun on the way, and in 433 was carried to Pingcheng and executed, while his son Yidu fled to the Liu Song and was granted the title of Prince of Yangshan. The last ruler of the Chouchi Di, whose name is given differently in the various histories and is recorded by some as Yang Yuan, surrendered with his people to the Northern Wei, and his clansmen were resettled inside Wei territory. On the Song side the government was in the hands of Emperor Wen of Song, Liu Yilong; in the tenth year of Yuanjia the court still relied on the northern-expedition commanders of the Tan Daoji circle, and the news of the loss of Hanzhong was precisely what came back to Jiankang from the northwest. There were also advisers such as Cui Hao, the Northern Wei grand secretary, but the histories do not record what part they actually played in this campaign, and the accounts differ.
kits: 卡面是公元前五世紀定型的希臘重步兵：青銅頭盔、短矛、圓盾與貼身甲胄，站位時盾牌相接，一個人靠鄰居的遮蔽活命。這套東西與本役無關，漢中谷道裡沒有任何希臘裝備；它值得放在這裡，是因為它標示了一種原理——以互相遮蔽換取正面厚度。實際上陣的是北魏的騎兵：人馬俱披甲，鐵槊、環首刀與角弓並用，當時尚未普遍使用馬鐙，鞍韜與披膊才是主體；步卒執大盾列陣，配長矛與弩，弩手多登城頭。攻城器械是雲梯、撞車與配重投石機，壕壘則以鹿角、拒馬與壞木壘塞河道。赫連大夏的裝備與胡族騎隊相混，長槍與弓箭並用，並有自製的甲騎；劉宋漢中守軍以弩為先，弓弩手居高臨下，步兵用大盾與長槍護住谷道。糧秣方面，漢中盆地有稻麥可食，但谷道狹窄，牛車難行，軍隊多靠人力背負與牛馬馱載；水路則可由漢水東下襄漢，運糧船可抵江陵一線。
kitsEn: The card shows a Greek hoplite as it was fixed in the fifth century BC: a bronze helmet, a short spear, a round shield and close-fitting body armour, standing so that shields touch, with each man alive only because his neighbour covers him. None of this had anything to do with the campaign: there was no Greek equipment in the Hanzhong gorges. It earns its place on the card because it marks a principle, that mutual cover is exchanged for a thicker front. What actually fought here was the cavalry of the Northern Wei: men and horses armoured, with iron spears, ring-pommel sabres and composite bows; stirrups were not yet in general use, and saddle and chamfron carried the armour. The infantry carried large shields and formed up with long spears and crossbows, the crossbowmen usually posted on the walls. The siege train was made of scaling ladders, rams and counterweight stone-throwers, while the lines were traced with deer-antler obstacles, caltrops and felled timber to dam the streams. The equipment of the Xia was mixed with that of the tribal horse columns, long spears and bows used together, with armoured riders of their own; the Song garrison of Hanzhong put the crossbow first, archers and crossbowmen up on the heights, and infantry with large shields and long spears to cover the gorge road. On supply: the Hanzhong basin grew rice and wheat, but the gorge was too narrow for ox carts, and the armies lived off what men and pack animals could carry; by water, grain could be taken down the Han river towards Xiangyang and on to the Yangtze, reaching the Jiangling line.
tactics: 秦嶺橫在漢中與關中之間，往來只靠褒斜、斜谷、陳倉三條谷道，每一條都容不下大隊人馬縱列推進，所以這場戰爭的樣貌不是會戰，而是斷糧與奪隘。魏軍的作法是分道：一部沿谷道進取漢中與仇池，一部直趨關中，騎兵先偵察隘口，步兵與輜重在後，奪路時以弩箭齊射先制，衝鋒則靠騎兵反覆掠奪城郊通道，不急於硬攻城牆。漢中與仇池一帶多山城小堡，魏軍多採圍而不攻、斷其樵汲的辦法，坐等守軍自潰。赫連定的夏軍則走的是相反的路子：430年襲平涼得手，靠的正是夜行奇襲與騎兵突進；433年他仍想用同一套本錢，先以偏師擾魏軍側翼，再圖長安，但夏的兵源分散在關中與隴右，一經失據便無後援。真正致命的一擊來自側後：吐谷渾騎兵切斷夏軍與隴西的聯繫，赫連定走投無路，才有了上邽的被擒。
tacticsEn: The Qinling range lies between Hanzhong and Guanzhong, and the two can be joined only by three gorge roads, the Baoxie, the Xiegu and the Chencang; not one of them will carry a long column of men, so the shape of this war was not a set-piece engagement but a contest over supply lines and passes. The Wei method was to split the army: one part took the gorge roads towards Hanzhong and Chouchi, another drove straight at Guanzhong; the cavalry scouted the defiles first, the infantry and baggage train followed, and when seizing a road the troops opened with a volley of crossbow bolts before the charge, while the horse worked the approaches to the town again and again, in no hurry to throw themselves against the walls. Around Hanzhong and Chouchi the country is full of small mountain strongholds, and the Wei habit was to surround rather than assault, cutting off firewood and water and waiting for the garrison to collapse of its own accord. Helian Ding's Xia army went the other way: its capture of Pingliang in 430 rested precisely on a night surprise and a cavalry rush, and in 433 it tried to spend the same coin, sending a detached force to harass the Wei flank and then aiming at Chang'an; but the Xia recruits were scattered across Guanzhong and Longyou, and once a position was lost there was no second line behind it. The blow that was truly fatal came from the rear: Tuyuhun horse cut the Xia army off from Longyou, and with nowhere to go Helian Ding was taken at Shanggui.
data: 可確定的只有年表與地理。赫連夏407年立國，433年亡國，凡二十六年；北魏在這二十六年裡，先於429年破柔然（斬首三萬餘級），再於432年遣拓跋仁率騎兵五萬伐北燕、進逼龍城，到433年才轉兵西南。433年這一年內，魏軍在隴右與關中連續用兵：仇池歸魏，漢中失守，赫連定兵敗長安，奔上邽，為吐谷渾所擒，於平城被誅；赫連宜都奔宋，封陽山公。地理上，漢中盆地南北狹長，與關中之間只隔三條谷道，漢中至長安是數百里山路，軍行、運糧與傳令都以旬日計，這就是《資治通鑑》所謂糧道艱阻的實情；自秦嶺北望關中，谷道盡處才有可以展開騎兵的寬地。兵員數字則不可考：《魏書》與《宋書》對此役只言師眾甚盛、大舉討平，具體兵數各書未載，本篇不湊數；唯一有數的是429年柔然之役的斬首三萬餘級與432年龍城之役的騎兵五萬，兩者都是別的戰役的數字，只能用來衡量北魏當時的兵力規模，不能移作本役的兵額。各書於月令亦互有出入，《宋書》繫於秋冬，《資治通鑑》分載於夏秋與秋，諸說並存。
dataEn: Only the chronology and the geography can be stated with certainty. The Xia was founded in 407 and destroyed in 433, a span of twenty-six years; across those same twenty-six years the Northern Wei first broke the Rouran in 429, with more than thirty thousand of them beheaded, then in 432 sent Tuoba Ren with fifty thousand cavalry against Northern Yan and pressed up to Longcheng, and only in 433 turned its army towards the southwest. Within that single year of 433 the Wei fought in Longyou and Guanzhong continuously: Chouchi went over to Wei, Hanzhong was lost, Helian Ding was beaten at Chang'an and fled to Shanggui, was taken by the Tuyuhun, and was executed at Pingcheng; Yindu fled to Song and was made Prince of Yangshan. Geographically, the Hanzhong basin is long and narrow from north to south, separated from Guanzhong by three gorge roads only, and the run from Hanzhong to Chang'an is several hundred li of mountain track, so that marching, supplying and despatching messages were all counted in tens of days; that is the reality behind the difficulty of the supply line noted in the Zizhi Tongjian. Looking north over the Qinling from Hanzhong, the only open ground wide enough to deploy cavalry in lies at the far end of the gorges. The numbers of men are simply not recoverable: the Wei Shu and the Song Shu say only that the host was very great and that the enemy was swept away in a great campaign, and the individual histories give no figures, so none are invented here. The only numbers that exist are the more than thirty thousand beheaded in the Rouran campaign of 429 and the fifty thousand cavalry of the Longcheng campaign of 432; both belong to other battles and can only be used to gauge the scale of the Wei armies of the time, not to serve as the troop strength of this one. The month is also given differently in the various histories, with the Song Shu placing it in the last part of the year and the Zizhi Tongjian spreading it across the summer and autumn.
cause: 打起來有兩層緣由。第一層是北魏的西進：拓跋燾要打通河西走廊與關中，把北涼、大夏、仇池這些割據的西北政權逐一收平，讓平城與涼州之間的路線真正歸於自己；柔然既破，429年他已把主力拉回，433年再向關中推進，是既定部署的延續。第二層是赫連夏自身的處境：夏在關中與隴右四面受敵，北有魏，西有涼，南有宋控制的漢中與梁州，一旦魏軍在漢中與仇池兩端落子，夏的後方便等於被掀開。赫連定因此先下手為強，430年趁魏主力在河南襲取平涼，433年又派太子宜都出擊魏境，敗後才被迫退守長安。此外，仇池楊氏在宋、魏、夏之間的兩面政策，把隴西南的局勢拉成了三國角力：楊氏一面以漢中太守的身分受宋之命，一面與夏往來，最終在魏軍壓力下率眾降魏，漢中隨即易手。劉宋則坐困於此：北伐主力遠在河南、淮北，漢中一旦有失，元嘉十年西線的部署便全盤散架。
causeEn: There are two layers of reason behind the fighting. The first is the Wei advance to the west: Taowu wanted to open the Hexi Corridor and Guanzhong into a single road, to subdue one after another the north-western states of Northern Liang, Xia and Chouchi, and to make the route between Pingcheng and Liangzhou genuinely his own; the Rouran were already broken, he had pulled the main army back in 429, and the push into Guanzhong in 433 was the continuation of a settled plan. The second is the Xia's own predicament: with the enemy on every side in Guanzhong and Longyou, the Wei to the north, Liang to the west, and the Song holding Hanzhong and Liangzhou to the south, the moment Wei troops appeared at both ends of the line, at Hanzhong and at Chouchi, the Xia rear was as good as turned open. Helian Ding therefore struck first, seizing Pingliang in 430 while the Wei main army stood in Henan, and in 433 he sent the crown prince Yidu out against Wei territory, and only after that failure was forced back to defend Chang'an. In addition, the two-faced policy of the Chouchi Di in Song, Wei and Xia turned southwestern Longyou into a three-way contest: the Yang clan, serving as commandant of Hanzhong under Song orders on one side and maintaining contacts with Xia on the other, finally surrendered with its people to Wei under military pressure, and Hanzhong changed hands at once. The Liu Song, for its part, was trapped by the situation: its expeditionary armies stood far away in Henan and north of the Huai, and once Hanzhong fell the western deployment of the tenth year of Yuanjia came apart entirely.
impact: 這一戰改變了西北三個國家的命運。大夏亡國，赫連氏退出歷史，關中與隴右盡入北魏，太武帝此後便能專心對付北涼，439年平姑臧、涼州五郡歸魏，450年再取統萬，至此北方大部分的黃河流域統一在拓跋氏手中，十六年後北魏分裂則是另外一段故事。對劉宋而言，漢中失守是元嘉之治最重的一次挫敗：秦嶺北面的屏障落到敵手，益州、荊州兩翼的壓力大增，宋從此放棄在西北的作為，北伐的鋒線收回到淮北與河南一線，元嘉末年朝政由盛轉衰、最終釀成元嘉三十年劉劭之亂，漢中易手正是這條下坡路的起點之一。對仇池楊氏而言，舉族降魏換來編戶齊民的地位，氐人從山谷政權的宗主變成魏國的編民，這條路後來又在關中與六鎮的鎮兵、部曲兵身上重演。對北魏而言，收編赫連宜都、封他為公、把他安置在宋境，也是拓跋燾慣用的手法：用敵國宗室在敵境內另立旗號，削弱其本國的號令；同一手法後來也用在沮渠氏與吐谷渾身上。赫連夏留下的兵制、屯田與築城技術，則被魏軍直接繼承，成為北魏在西北立國的骨架。
impactEn: This war changed the fortunes of three states in the north-west. The Xia was destroyed, the Hulian clan disappeared from history, and Guanzhong and Longyou passed entirely to the Northern Wei; Taowu could then concentrate on Northern Liang, taking the capital Guzang in 439 so that the five Hexi commanderies came over, and returning to Tongwan in 450, by which time the greater part of the Yellow River basin in the north was in the hands of the Tuoba clan; the collapse of Northern Wei sixteen years later is a different story. For the Liu Song, the loss of Hanzhong was the gravest reverse of the Yuanjia age: the screen north of the Qinling fell into enemy hands, the pressure on the two wings of Yizhou and Jingzhou grew sharply, and the Song gave up what it had been attempting in the north-west, drawing the edge of its northern expeditions back to the Huai and Henan. As the government of the late Yuanjia years turned from strength to weakness and finally produced the rebellion of Liu Shao in the thirtieth year, the change of hands at Hanzhong was one of the first steps down that slope. For the Chouchi Di, surrendering with the clan bought them the status of registered commoners: the Di went from being lords of a mountain state to being subjects on the Wei register, a road later walked again by the garrison troops and the dependent bands of Guanzhong and the six garrisons. For the Northern Wei, taking over Yidu, granting him a title and settling him inside Song territory was a habitual device of Taowu's: setting up a member of a hostile royal house under a flag of his own in the enemy's country to weaken the authority of that enemy's own government; the same device was later used with the Juqu and with the Tuyuhun. The military system, the garrison farms and the fortification methods that the Xia had developed were taken over directly by the Wei armies and became the skeleton of the Wei state in the north-west.
result: 結果很明確：赫連定兵敗長安，奔上邽，為吐谷渾所擒，433年送抵平城被誅，大夏國亡；仇池楊氏率眾降魏，漢中歸魏，關中與隴右的門戶洞開；赫連宜都奔投劉宋，被封陽山公，成為宋用以誇示北方的政治籌碼，也說明大夏宗室在西北已無立錐之地。回頭看卡面：公元前五世紀的希臘重步兵一次也沒有出現在漢中谷道裡，而且它原理上也不可能適用——方陣要靠開闊的正面才成立，褒斜、斜谷、陳倉三道都是狹長谷地，一展開便是送死；這場戰爭真正決定勝負的，是騎兵、弩、投石機與糧道，是大夏名將赫連勃勃在亂軍之中陣亡所留下的那種混亂，而漢中的城頭靠的是弩手與礌石，不是互相遮蔽的盾牌。本戰役的記載零散，各書於兵數、月份與交鋒細節互有出入，諸說並存；此處只依可以確定的年表與地理立說，不替諸說補數字。
resultEn: The outcome was clear enough: Helian Ding was beaten at Chang'an, fled to Shanggui, was taken by the Tuyuhun, and in 433 was carried to Pingcheng and executed, and the state of Xia was destroyed; the Yang clan of Chouchi surrendered with its people to the Wei, Hanzhong passed to the north, and the door into Guanzhong and Longyou stood wide open; Yindu fled to the Liu Song and was made Prince of Yangshan, becoming a political token with which the Song vaunted itself before the north, and at the same time showing that the Xia royal house had no place left to stand in the north-west. Returning to the card: the Greek hoplite of the fifth century BC never once appeared in the gorges of Hanzhong, and could not in principle have applied, for a phalanx only works with a broad front, and the Baoxie, Xiegu and Chencang roads are all narrow defiles where opening up means dying. What really decided this war was cavalry, crossbows, stone-throwers and the supply line; it was the kind of confusion left behind by the death of the great Xia commander Helian Bobo in the midst of a confused battle; and the walls of Hanzhong were held by crossbowmen and stones, not by shields that covered one another. The record of this campaign is scattered, and the histories differ over numbers, months and the details of the fighting, so the accounts stand side by side; here only the chronology and the geography that can be relied upon have been used, and no figures have been supplied to patch up the competing versions.
